units.length_in_glb: For earth_*.glb, 1 unit = 1 Earth radius = R_E.
units.satellite_glbs: iss, hubble, gps, geo_comsat are in meters, origin at mesh center, Y-up.
units.moon_glb: moon_*.glb has radius 1 = 1 lunar radius (1,737.4 km, LRO/LOLA reference). Scale by (1737.4 / 6380) relative to earth_*.glb.

constants.notes: Tesla-verified unit values. Do not change GM_E or R_E.

formulas.r: r is measured from Earth's center. For a circular orbit, r = R_E + altitude.

surface.name: Earth surface
surface.notes: Mean radius used in the unit, not the IAU equatorial radius.

ISS.name: ISS
ISS.notes: Altitude 400 km is the unit value.

Hubble.name: Hubble Space Telescope
Hubble.g_N_per_kg_note: Tesla-verified teaching value; g_N_per_kg_computed uses g=GM_E/r^2.
Hubble.notes: Altitude 480 km and g=8.46 N/kg are Tesla-verified teaching values.

GEO.name: Geostationary
GEO.period_h_note: Tesla-verified teaching value; period_h_computed uses T=2π√(r³/GM_E).
GEO.notes: r=42,145 km from Earth's center and T=23.93 h are Tesla-verified teaching values (sidereal day), not altitude above the surface.

Moon.name: Moon (mean distance)
Moon.notes: For the Lesson 4 Scale Walk. Mean distance 384,400 km and sidereal period 27.3217 days are from the NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html. period_s_computed uses the circular two-body formula with the unit GM_E and this mean distance; it is close to, but not identical to, the sidereal month (the real orbit is slightly eccentric and around the barycenter). R_E = 6.38e6 m is the unit value, so r/R_E is about 60.25. Do not display a g readout during the Lesson 4 S6 task.

GPS.name: GPS (typical circular MEO)
GPS.notes: Not a Tesla-verified unit constant. Typical GPS altitude of 20,180 km (about 20,200 km is also commonly quoted). Period and g are computed from GM_E and R_E so students can compare LEO, GPS, and GEO. Cite as a typical operational altitude, e.g. GPS program documentation / NASA GPS overview.

lesson_presets.L1_S8_suborbital_lob: Orbit Lab starting at Newton's cannon, slow horizontal lob that hits the ground. Stay suborbital. Use newton_cannon.glb.
lesson_presets.L4_S6_scale_walk: Earth with ISS orbit at 400 km true scale (R_E=6.38e6 m). Hubble at 480 km may be shown as a second low ring. Include the Moon at 384,400 km if you show the Scale Walk distance. Turn off or ignore g and period readouts. Do not have students record a g value.
lesson_presets.L5_S8_newtons_cannon: Newton's cannon on the mountain, horizontal launch, increasing speeds from a lob to the shot that never lands. Use newton_cannon.glb.
lesson_presets.L5_S12_optional_orbits: Presets for ISS (400 km), GPS (typical 20,180 km), and GEO (r=42,145 km, T=23.93 h).
